newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Qantas, BA expand alliance network.
newsitem.headline: Qantas, BA expand alliance network.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd said on Thursday its alliance with major shareholder British Airways Plc will enter a new phase through the expansion of their networks in Europe and Australia by more codesharing on some flights.
Qantas will extend its network in the United Kingdom to include an additional five cities, Manchester, belfast, Edinburgh, Glasgow and Aberdeen, the Australian airline said.
These services - operated by British Airways - would connect with the twice daily Qantas fliights to London from Australia, Singapore and Bangkok, Qantas said.
Qantas would also broaden its network in continental Europe through codesharing on British Airways flights, with the addition of Vienna, Amsterdam and Paris, it said.
It said the services to Austria and the Netherlands are subject to final government approval.

The increases have been made possible through an agreement in which Qantas will sell seats on selected British Airways flights to cities in the UK and Europe, and British Airways will sell seats on selected Qantas flights in Australia, said Qantas.
British Airways would expand its reach in Australia with the introduction of codeshare on 70 Qantas flights per week to Sydney, Adelaide, Canberra, Coolangatta, Melbourne, Hobart and Perth.
Qantas is 25 percent owned by British Airways.
